task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-08-08, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Cut-heavy shapers' roles travel better than drive-heavy ones.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=24

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: Shaper role (low usage, positive residual structural influence)
Role portability across teams (movers between seasons)
methodological_questions: How is 'travel' operationalised: retained shaper label, retained residual influence, or retained initiation mix?
Can 24 units separate cut-heavy from drive-heavy shapers at useful power?
Is the cut-heavy/drive-heavy split defined independently of the outcome measure?
How much apparent persistence difference is regression to the mean from selecting shapers on residual influence?
How to handle team context, teammates, minutes and usage changes after a move, and how to calibrate against decoys?
evidence_establishes: Nothing: retrieve_history returned no records, so no historical evidence was available for this question.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether this or a similar portability question was previously tested, supported, rejected or found untestable.
Whether the project's shaper or mover definitions are reliable enough for this comparison.
Any prior estimate of variance or effect size for role persistence among movers.
own_inferences: The glossary defines a Shaper by a median split on usage and a residual-influence sign, and defines movers and decoys, so the 24 units are probably mover-shapers. This is unconfirmed.
Splitting 24 units into cut-heavy and drive-heavy groups leaves roughly 12 per arm or fewer. That only detects very large differences (about d ≥ 1.2) and is fragile to any unbalanced split.

Selecting shapers on a positive residual makes regression to the mean likely, so both groups will look less shaper-like after a move. A group difference could arise if the two profiles differ in measurement noise, because cut initiations are rarer and noisier than drives.
A cut-heavy role depends on teammates' passing and spacing, so it could travel worse as easily as better. The direction is not obvious a priori.
Cut-heavy versus drive-heavy is probably correlated with position, usage, and the destination team's style, which confounds the comparison.
Drive-heavy and cut-heavy may be defined from the same initiation records that give the persistence outcome, creating a shared-label dependence.
uncertainties: Exact definition of 'travel' and 'cut-heavy/drive-heavy' (thresholds) is not given.
What the 24 units are, and how many fall in each profile, is unknown.
Classifier accuracy for CUT and DRIVE labels is unknown.
Minimum possession counts per player-season are unknown, so the reliability of per-player mixes is unknown.
Whether 2025-26 data being complete changes the sample is unclear; the stated n=24 may or may not include it.

historical_effect.explanation: No records were returned, so the decision rests only on the task statement, the glossary, and general methodological reasoning. Nothing in the decision comes from earlier project results.

blocking_constraints.text: n=24 split into two profile groups gives about 12 per arm, with power only for very large differences.
Shapers are selected on high residual influence, so post-move regression to the mean is expected and may differ by profile.
Per-player CUT and DRIVE shares and residual influence may be noisy at the possession counts available, especially after a move to a new team.

prior_work.summary: No earlier work was retrieved, so it is unknown whether this question was studied. No claim is made about earlier studies.

risks.text: Roughly 12 units per profile; wide intervals; a dichotomised comparison discards information.
Selection on the pre-move shaper label (positive residual) guarantees some regression; compare against decoys or non-selected controls.
Cut shares are sparse and noisy. Persistence metrics (cosine similarity, label retention) have different reliabilities by profile.
Profile and persistence both come from the same initiation records; define profile on pre-move seasons only and outcome on post-move seasons only.
Destination team style, teammate quality, position, usage change, minutes and coaching changes differ across movers.
Rule-based CUT and DRIVE classification from play-by-play text may misclassify possessions, differentially by profile.
Decoy matches depend on matching quality; poor decoys would misstate the baseline portability.
Several persistence metrics, thresholds and season pairs invite forking paths unless fixed in advance.
Three season transitions with league-wide play-type drift; regular season versus playoff mix differences.
The median split and the sign-based label can create threshold effects: shapers near the cutoff lose the label by small changes.

design.estimand: Difference in post-move retention of shaper-type structure between cut-heavy and drive-heavy shapers, primarily the continuous association between pre-move cut share minus drive share and post-move persistence (cosine similarity of the player's initiation mix across the move, and the post-move residual influence), net of a decoy-based baseline. A dichotomised contrast is secondary.
design.unit: Mover-shaper (player moving teams between consecutive seasons, with shaper status in the pre-move season).
design.sample: All qualifying mover-shapers across the transitions 2022-23→2023-24, 2023-24→2024-25 and 2024-25→2025-26 (regular season, playoffs reported separately), n=24 as recorded. Fix minimum possessions per player-season before looking at outcomes. Report the number of units in each profile before analysis.
design.power: With about 12 per arm only large effects (d ≈ 1.2) reach 80% power. Treat the study as estimation with confidence intervals; no confirmatory claim of a difference unless the interval excludes zero and the effect is large. If the pre-registered profile split is below 8 per arm, report as descriptive only.
design.controls: Profile and shaper label from pre-move season only; persistence from post-move season only. Compare to matched decoys (non-moving, same-team-profile players) to estimate regression to the mean and to establish baseline persistence. Adjust for pre-move usage, position, minutes, destination team's CUT/DRIVE mix, and teammate change. Use a bootstrap or permutation test at the unit level. Check that CUT and DRIVE classification is stable by hand audit of a sample.
design.falsification: Placebo test: apply the same cut-heavy versus drive-heavy contrast to decoys who stayed with their teams; a similar gap would indicate measurement or selection artifact rather than portability. Also rerun with the profile labels randomly permuted and with a different threshold for cut-heavy.
design.multiplicity: One primary outcome (cosine similarity of initiation mix), one primary contrast (continuous cut-minus-drive share), fixed thresholds. Other metrics (label retention, residual influence), playoffs and thresholds are secondary and labelled exploratory with Holm correction.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if the primary effect is positive, the 95% interval excludes zero after decoy adjustment, and the placebo contrast on decoys is near zero. Rejected only if the interval excludes effects of practical size in the claimed direction with at least 8 per arm. Otherwise report inconclusive; do not claim that cut-heavy roles travel better.
design.data_version: Per-game NBA stats API files and derived play-type graph as of 2026-08-08 (2025-26 regular season and playoffs complete); freeze the data snapshot, classifier version and threshold definitions before analysis.
